```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE}
.mod_meta <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hishe_2023_oxypurinol"))
```

* Citation: `r .mod_meta$meta$reference`
* Description: `r .mod_meta$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13460>

The packaged model implements the Hishe 2023 final covariate model of oxypurinol
(the active metabolite of allopurinol) population pharmacokinetics in adults with
gout, pooled across five New Zealand studies and fitted in NONMEM 7.3 (FOCE-I).
The structural model is one-compartment with first-order absorption (Ka fixed at
0.993 1/h) and first-order elimination. Apparent oral clearance CL/F is
power-scaled on Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance standardised to 70 kg
(`CRCL`, in L/h, reference 6 L/h), reduced multiplicatively by concomitant
diuretic use (`CONMED_DIURETIC`), raised multiplicatively in Pacific peoples
(`RACE_PACIFIC`), and power-scaled on total body weight (`WT`); apparent volume
V/F is linearly weight-scaled. A separate combined additive + proportional
residual error was estimated for each of the five studies, selected by the
`STUDY_*` indicator columns (Study 5 / Stamp 2017, the largest sub-cohort, is the
all-zeros reference). Seven urate-transporter gene variants were screened but
none were retained in the final model.

The dose entered into the model is oral allopurinol in mg. Only oxypurinol
concentrations were measured, so bioavailability, the paper's 0.9
allopurinol-to-oxypurinol conversion factor and the molar conversion are absorbed
into the apparent CL/F and V/F; the observation `Cc` is oxypurinol concentration
in umol/L (see Assumptions for the molar-vs-mass reading of the 0.9 factor).

# Population

Hishe 2023 fit the model to 2841 plasma oxypurinol concentrations from 300 adults
with gout (264 male / 36 female; sex-female 12%) pooled across five New Zealand
studies conducted in Christchurch and Auckland. The cohort was middle-aged to
elderly (age range 23-86 years, median 61), heavy (total body weight range
51-186 kg, median 102 kg) and spanned a wide range of renal function
(Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 8-167 mL/min, median 63 mL/min). Allopurinol
doses ranged 50-900 mg/day (median 300 mg/day). By ethnicity the cohort was 59%
European / NZ European, 21% Pacific peoples, 16% Maori, 2% Chinese, 2% Indian and
1% Other; 37% were on a concomitant diuretic. The full demographic summary appears
in Hishe 2023 Table S4; the transporter genotype distribution is in Table 1.

The same metadata is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Hishe_2023_oxypurinol")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Hishe_2023_oxypurinol.R`. The table below
collects them in one place for review. All point estimates are from Hishe 2023
Table 2 ("Final model" column); the structural layout and covariate
parameterisation are from the Results equations and the Appendix S2 NONMEM
control stream.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (Ka) | fixed(log(0.993)) | Table 2 row "ka"; Appendix S2 `$THETA` `0.993 FIX` |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | log(0.97) -> 0.97 L/h | Table 2 row "thetaCL"; bootstrap 0.97 [0.88-1.06] |
| `lvc` (V/F) | log(49) -> 49 L | Table 2 row "thetaV"; bootstrap 49 [43-54] |
| `e_crcl_cl` (thetaRFexp) | 0.58 | Table 2 row "thetaRFexp"; bootstrap 0.58 [0.49-0.66] |
| `e_conmed_diuretic_cl` (thetad) | 0.79 | Table 2 row "thetaddiuretic"; bootstrap 0.79 [0.74-0.85]; -21% on CL |
| `e_race_pacific_cl` (thetae) | 1.25 | Table 2 row "thetaeethnicity"; bootstrap 1.25 [1.12-1.37]; +25% on CL |
| `e_wt_cl` (thetaWTexp) | 0.34 | Table 2 row "thetaWTexp"; bootstrap 0.35 [0.17-0.53] |
| `e_wt_vc` | fixed(1.0) | Results equation `V/F = thetaV * (WT/70)`; no Table 2 exponent row |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.298^2 = 0.088804 | Table 2 row "omega CL CV%" = 29.8% (as log-SD; see Assumptions) |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.413^2 = 0.170569 | Table 2 row "omega V CV%" = 41.3% |
| `etalcl` x `etalvc` cov | 0.41 * sqrt(0.088804 * 0.170569) = 0.050464 | Table 2 row "Corr omega CL, omega V" = 0.41 |
| `etalka` variance | fixed(0.388) | Table 2 "omega Ka CV%" 62.3% (fixed); Appendix S2 `$OMEGA` `0.388 FIX` |
| `addSd_s1` / `propSd_s1` | fixed(0.0001) / 0.435 | Table 2 Study 1 residual error |
| `addSd_s2` / `propSd_s2` | 10.0 / fixed(0.0001) | Table 2 Study 2 residual error |
| `addSd_s3` / `propSd_s3` | fixed(0.0001) / 0.422 | Table 2 Study 3 residual error |
| `addSd_s4` / `propSd_s4` | 0.93 / 0.348 | Table 2 Study 4 residual error |
| `addSd_s5` / `propSd_s5` | fixed(0.0001) / 0.485 | Table 2 Study 5 residual error |
| CL/F equation | `thetaCL * (CRCL/6)^0.58 * 0.79^DIURETIC * 1.25^PACIFIC * (WT/70)^0.34` | Results covariate-model equation; Appendix S2 `$PK` |
| V/F equation | `thetaV * (WT/70)` | Results covariate-model equation |
| ODE `d/dt(depot)` | `-ka * depot` | One-compartment first-order absorption (Appendix S1 base model) |
| ODE `d/dt(central)` | `ka * depot - kel * central` | Same |
| Observation `Cc` | `0.9 * central / vc * 1000 / 136.11` | 0.9 conversion factor (Appendix S1) x molar conversion with allopurinol MW 136.11 |

# Virtual cohort

Original observed concentration-time data are not publicly available. The vignette
builds two virtual populations against which the packaged model is validated.

**Cohort A -- a representative pooled cohort** (n = 200) with covariates sampled to
approximate the Hishe 2023 Table S4 marginal distributions: log-normal body weight
(median 102 kg), log-normal creatinine clearance (median 63 mL/min, i.e. 3.78 L/h
standardised to 70 kg), 37% on a diuretic and 21% Pacific peoples. This cohort
carries the model's full between-subject and residual variability and is used for
the steady-state VPC and the NCA.

**Cohort B -- covariate-effect strata** (typical-value, random effects zeroed): a
small set of one-at-a-time covariate contrasts used to confirm the Table 2
clearance covariate multipliers exactly.

All subjects receive once-daily oral allopurinol 300 mg (the cohort median) for
14 days to reach approximate steady state; concentrations are observed densely
across the final dosing interval. All `STUDY_*` indicators are left at 0, so the
residual error is that of Study 5 (Stamp 2017, the largest sub-cohort and the
reference level).

```{r cohort}
# `set.seed()` seeds R's RNG for the covariate draws below; it does NOT seed
# rxode2's per-thread simulation RNG, so the realised cohort differs across
# machines with different thread counts. Every assertion downstream is written
# to hold for any cohort the model can produce (centre + robust bounds), per
# the repository's vignette-assertion guidance.
set.seed(20230314)

mod_full    <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hishe_2023_oxypurinol"))
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_full)

dose_mg   <- 300    # cohort median allopurinol dose (mg/day)
tau       <- 24     # dosing interval (h)
n_doses   <- 14L    # 14 daily doses to reach steady state
n_per_arm <- 200L

ref_crcl <- 6       # L/h (normalisation standard = 100 mL/min/70 kg)
ref_wt   <- 70

# Log-normal covariate draws calibrated to the Table S4 medians and ranges.
# CRCL is stored in L/h standardised to 70 kg: the cohort median 63 mL/min
# corresponds to 63 * 0.06 = 3.78 L/h.
make_subjects <- function(n, id_offset = 0L) {
  tibble(
    id  = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT  = round(stats::rlnorm(n, log(102), 0.22), 1),
    CRCL = round(pmax(0.5, stats::rlnorm(n, log(3.78), 0.45)), 2),
    CONMED_DIURETIC = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.37),
    RACE_PACIFIC    = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.21),
    STUDY_STAMP2011 = 0L, STUDY_STAMP2012 = 0L,
    STUDY_STAMP2013 = 0L, STUDY_WRIGHT2016 = 0L
  )
}

expand_events <- function(subjects, n_doses, tau, dose_mg) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(id = subjects$id, dose_idx = seq_len(n_doses)) |>
    mutate(time = (dose_idx - 1L) * tau, evid = 1L,
           cmt = "depot", amt = dose_mg) |>
    select(-dose_idx) |>
    left_join(subjects, by = "id")
  obs_start <- (n_doses - 1L) * tau
  obs_grid  <- c(seq(obs_start, obs_start + tau - 1, by = 0.5), obs_start + tau)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = subjects$id, time = obs_grid) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_) |>
    left_join(subjects, by = "id")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

subjects_A <- make_subjects(n_per_arm)
events_A   <- expand_events(subjects_A, n_doses, tau, dose_mg)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_A[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

# Cohort B: covariate-effect contrasts at the reference covariate state.
contrasts_B <- tibble::tribble(
  ~stratum,        ~CRCL, ~WT, ~CONMED_DIURETIC, ~RACE_PACIFIC,
  "reference",       6,   70,              0L,            0L,
  "+diuretic",       6,   70,              1L,            0L,
  "+Pacific",        6,   70,              0L,            1L,
  "CRCL 3 L/h",      3,   70,              0L,            0L,
  "WT 100 kg",       6,  100,              0L,            0L
)
subjects_B <- contrasts_B |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()),
         STUDY_STAMP2011 = 0L, STUDY_STAMP2012 = 0L,
         STUDY_STAMP2013 = 0L, STUDY_WRIGHT2016 = 0L)
events_B <- expand_events(subjects_B, n_doses, tau, dose_mg)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_A <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_full, events = events_A,
  keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "CONMED_DIURETIC", "RACE_PACIFIC"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

sim_B <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical, events = events_B,
  keep = c("stratum", "WT", "CRCL", "CONMED_DIURETIC", "RACE_PACIFIC"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Steady-state VPC (Hishe 2023 Figure 1 context)

Hishe 2023 Figure 1 is a visual predictive check of plasma oxypurinol against time
from the start of each study, showing the model-predicted median and 5th / 95th
percentiles tracking the observed percentiles. The original uses the observed
sampling design, which is not public; the chunk below shows the comparable
model-predicted VPC band over the final steady-state dosing interval for the
representative cohort.

```{r fig1-vpc, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.5}
sim_A_num <- sim_A |> mutate(time = as.numeric(time))
obs_start <- (n_doses - 1L) * tau

vpc_band <- sim_A_num |>
  mutate(time_in_interval = time - obs_start) |>
  group_by(time_in_interval) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_band, aes(time_in_interval, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, colour = "steelblue4") +
  labs(x = "Time after final dose (h)",
       y = "Plasma oxypurinol concentration (umol/L)",
       title = "Steady-state oxypurinol VPC, representative cohort (300 mg/day)",
       caption = paste("Model-predicted 5th/50th/95th percentiles over the",
                       "final dosing interval; VPC context of Hishe 2023",
                       "Figure 1."))
```

## Clearance covariate effects (Hishe 2023 Table 2)

The typical-value (random-effects-zeroed) individual clearance recovered for each
covariate contrast reproduces the Table 2 multipliers exactly: diuretic 0.79,
Pacific 1.25, and the renal / weight power terms.

```{r cov-effects}
cl_B <- sim_B |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(cl = dplyr::first(cl), .groups = "drop")
ref_cl <- cl_B$cl[cl_B$stratum == "reference"]

cov_tab <- cl_B |>
  mutate(ratio_vs_ref = cl / ref_cl,
         expected = dplyr::case_when(
           stratum == "reference"  ~ 1,
           stratum == "+diuretic"  ~ 0.79,
           stratum == "+Pacific"   ~ 1.25,
           stratum == "CRCL 3 L/h" ~ (3 / 6)^0.58,
           stratum == "WT 100 kg"  ~ (100 / 70)^0.34
         ))

knitr::kable(
  cov_tab |>
    dplyr::rename("Stratum" = stratum, "CL (L/h)" = cl,
                  "Ratio vs reference" = ratio_vs_ref,
                  "Expected (Table 2)" = expected),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Typical-value CL by covariate contrast vs the Hishe 2023 Table 2 multipliers."
)

# The covariate multipliers are deterministic functions of the ini() estimates,
# so they must match to numerical tolerance.
stopifnot(all(abs(cov_tab$ratio_vs_ref - cov_tab$expected) < 1e-6))
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the representative cohort over the final 24-h steady-state dosing
interval, re-anchored to time = 0. Dose / AUC0-tau recovers the apparent
oxypurinol clearance CL/F, which is compared against the Hishe 2023 typical-value
thetaCL = 0.97 L/h after accounting for the cohort covariate distribution.

```{r pknca}
last_dose_time <- (n_doses - 1L) * tau
nca_conc <- sim_A_num |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= last_dose_time, time <= last_dose_time + tau) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = time - last_dose_time) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))

# Time-zero anchor: the observation grid starts exactly at the final dose, so
# every subject already has a t = 0 row (the steady-state trough, not zero).
stopifnot(all(tapply(nca_conc$time, nca_conc$id, min) == 0))

# Oxypurinol-equivalent dose in umol, so dose / AUC (umol/L) gives CL in L/h.
dose_umol <- 0.9 * dose_mg / 136.11 * 1000
nca_dose <- nca_conc |>
  dplyr::distinct(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_umol)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | id, concu = "umol/L", timeu = "hr")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | id, doseu = "umol")

intervals_ss <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_ss))
knitr::kable(
  summary(nca_ss),
  caption = paste("Steady-state NCA over the final 24-h interval,",
                  "representative cohort (full BSV + residual error).")
)
```

## Comparison against the published model

Hishe 2023 does not report a non-compartmental Cmax / AUC table, so the validation
compares the recovered apparent clearance and the cohort steady-state exposure
against the published structural quantities: thetaCL = 0.97 L/h (typical patient
at the reference covariate state) and the observed median plasma oxypurinol of
112 umol/L (Table S4).

```{r nca_compare}
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_ss$result)
auc_per_id <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, auc_tau = PPORRES)
cl_per_id <- auc_per_id |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl_recovered = dose_umol / auc_tau)

# Typical-value CL/F at the reference covariate state, from the deterministic
# contrast simulation (thetaCL with all covariates at reference = 0.97 L/h).
cl_ref_typ <- cl_B$cl[cl_B$stratum == "reference"]

# Cohort median steady-state oxypurinol concentration.
cohort_med_css <- median(sim_A_num$Cc[sim_A_num$time >= last_dose_time], na.rm = TRUE)

summary_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Typical CL/F at reference covariates (L/h)",
               "Cohort median steady-state Cc (umol/L)"),
  Simulated = c(round(cl_ref_typ, 3), round(cohort_med_css, 1)),
  Published = c(0.97, 112)
)
knitr::kable(summary_tab, caption = "Simulated vs Hishe 2023 published quantities.")

# Structural checks.
# (1) The typical CL/F at the reference covariate state IS thetaCL by
#     construction, so it must equal 0.97 L/h to numerical tolerance.
stopifnot(abs(cl_ref_typ - 0.97) < 1e-3)

# (2) The cohort-level CL recovered by NCA (median) should track the covariate-
#     weighted typical CL. A mis-transcribed CL, dose or unit would move the
#     whole distribution by tens of percent; the bound is generous enough to be
#     robust to which subjects land in the tails but tight enough to catch a
#     structural error.
#     Observed across renders: about 0.9 L/h.
med_cl_recovered <- median(cl_per_id$cl_recovered, na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(med_cl_recovered > 0.65, med_cl_recovered < 1.25)

# (3) The cohort steady-state exposure should bracket the observed median
#     (112 umol/L) within a physiologically plausible envelope. This is a
#     different quantity (median of sampled concentrations across a mixed
#     cohort vs the paper's observed median), so a wide structural bound is
#     used rather than a tight one. Observed across renders: about 90 umol/L.
stopifnot(cohort_med_css > 60, cohort_med_css < 160)
```

The typical CL/F at the reference covariate state equals thetaCL by construction.
The representative cohort's median steady-state oxypurinol concentration (about
90 umol/L at 300 mg/day) sits below the observed median of 112 umol/L in Table
S4. The observed median pools samples across doses of 50-900 mg/day, real
sampling times and correlated covariates (lower doses are given in renal
impairment), none of which the virtual cohort reproduces, so it is only an
approximate anchor; see the Assumptions for how it bears on the dose conversion.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Allopurinol-to-oxypurinol conversion (molar reading).** Only oxypurinol was
  measured; the paper relates the allopurinol dose to oxypurinol with a 0.9
  conversion factor (Hishe 2023 Appendix S1, citing Day 2007). The packaged model
  applies this as a **molar** conversion: 0.9 of the allopurinol molecules become
  oxypurinol (1:1 molar), so `Cc = 0.9 * central / vc * 1000 / 136.11` (umol/L),
  using the allopurinol molecular weight 136.11 g/mol. This is the physically
  correct reading of a conversion fraction, matches the same research group's
  parent-metabolite convention (`Wright_2013_allopurinol.R`), and is the closer
  of the two readings to the observed data: the representative cohort's median
  steady-state concentration is about 90 umol/L under the molar reading and
  about 80 umol/L under the mass reading, against the observed median of
  112 umol/L (Table S4). The maintainers
  considered a **mass** reading (0.9 * mg allopurinol taken as mg oxypurinol, then
  divided by the oxypurinol molecular weight 152.11), which is how the cited
  origin of the 0.9 factor (Day 2007) and the sibling `Stocker_2012_oxypurinol.R`
  express the relationship; that reading predicts concentrations about 12% lower
  (the molecular-weight ratio 152.11/136.11). The paper does not state which
  molecular weight turned the allopurinol dose into the NONMEM oxypurinol amount,
  so the 12% band is a genuine ambiguity; the molar reading was chosen on the
  closer agreement with the observed median and the within-group precedent.
- **Between-subject variability reported as log-scale SD.** Hishe 2023 Table 2
  reports omega as "CV%". The Appendix S2 control stream fixes the Ka variance at
  omega^2 = 0.388, and sqrt(0.388) = 0.623 = the reported 62.3% CV, confirming
  that the printed "CV%" is the log-scale standard deviation expressed as a
  percentage (the NONMEM-tradition CV ~= omega). The packaged model therefore
  encodes omega^2 = (CV%/100)^2 for CL (29.8%), V (41.3%) and Ka (62.3%), with the
  CL/V covariance from the reported correlation 0.41.
- **Per-study residual error and the reference study.** A separate combined
  additive + proportional residual error was estimated for each of the five pooled
  studies (Table 2). The packaged model selects the per-study error via the
  `STUDY_STAMP2011` / `STUDY_STAMP2012` / `STUDY_STAMP2013` / `STUDY_WRIGHT2016`
  indicator columns; when all four are 0 the error defaults to Study 5 (Stamp
  2017), the largest sub-cohort (176 of 300). This vignette leaves all four at 0,
  so the VPC and NCA use the Study-5 residual.
- **Creatinine clearance units.** `CRCL` is Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance
  standardised to 70 kg and expressed in L/h (normalisation standard 6 L/h = 100
  mL/min/70 kg), matching the sibling `Wright_2016_allopurinol.R`. The virtual
  cohort draws `CRCL` in L/h (cohort median 3.78 L/h = 63 mL/min).
- **Volume weight exponent fixed.** The Results equation writes `V/F = thetaV *
  (WT/70)` with no exponent reported in Table 2, so the weight exponent on volume
  is held fixed at the theoretical value 1.0 (linear).
- **Urate-transporter genotypes not modelled.** Seven SNPs (ABCG2 rs2231142 and
  rs10011796, SLC2A9 rs11942223, SLC17A1 rs1183201, SLC22A12 rs3825018, SLC22A11
  rs17300741, ABCC4 rs4148500) were screened. ABCG2 rs2231142 (+24%) and SLC17A1
  rs1183201 (+22%) were significant univariately but not retained in the
  multivariate model, where they were confounded by correlated creatinine
  clearance, weight, age, diuretic use and ethnicity. The packaged model has no
  SNP covariates; the screened variants are recorded in the model file's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
- **Virtual-cohort distributions.** The covariate distributions are log-normal
  approximations to the Hishe 2023 Table S4 marginals (weight, creatinine
  clearance) with independent 37% diuretic and 21% Pacific prevalences; the
  original per-subject covariate data are not public, so inter-covariate
  correlations (e.g. the reported association of the ABCG2 T allele with higher
  CrCl, lower diuretic use and Pacific ethnicity) are not reproduced.
- **Errata.** No erratum or corrigendum to Hishe 2023 was found in the sources on
  hand as of this writing (2026-10); the maintainers should reconfirm against the
  Clinical and Translational Science corrections feed if a re-extraction is
  undertaken.
